name: Frame Drop Detection
description: Detects frame continuity breaks and drop patterns common in AI-generated video
algorithm: Frame Drop Detection — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method detects anomalous frame drops and timing irregularities for deepfake detection:

1. **Frame Timing Analysis**: Presentation timestamps (PTS) and decode timestamps (DTS) are analyzed for timing regularity. Authentic video shows consistent frame intervals matching the declared frame rate (±encoder tolerance). Manipulated video may show timing anomalies from frame insertion, deletion, or re-timing.

2. **Optical Flow Frame Interpolation Check**: Inter-frame optical flow magnitude is analyzed. Dropped frames produce larger-than-expected optical flow between surviving frames (double the normal inter-frame motion). The method detects statistically anomalous flow magnitudes indicating missing frames.

3. **Temporal Artifact Detection**: Frame drops produce specific visual artifacts: (a) motion judder (uneven motion appearance), (b) temporal aliasing (fast-moving objects show irregular positions), (c) audio-video desync accumulation. The method detects these artifacts as indicators of temporal manipulation.

4. **Selective Frame Drop Pattern**: Natural frame drops (from capture issues) are typically random. Deepfake manipulation may show selective frame drops — specifically removing frames containing generation artifacts or temporal inconsistencies. The method analyzes frame drop patterns for non-random distributions correlated with content complexity or face presence.

5. **Re-Timing Detection**: Video that has been re-timed (frame rate converted) shows characteristic blend frames or frame selection patterns. The method detects re-timing signatures that may indicate the video has been processed through a deepfake pipeline that outputs at a different frame rate than the source.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through frame drop detection analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
